title: The Scientist Who Was Called 'Harriet' When All the Men Were 'Doctor'
summary: Have you ever been the only kid in a group who loves something different? Harriet Robinson knows exactly how that feels. Back in the 1960s, she was often the only woman scientist in a room full of men. While they were called 'Doctor' or 'Professor,' everyone just called her 'Harriet.' But Harriet didn't let that stop her. She went on to do amazing things! As a kid, Harriet loved learning, especially history and languages. She even worked as a Russian-English guide at a big exhibition in Moscow, standing next to a shiny Ford Thunderbird while wearing a flight attendant's uniform. How cool is that? But her real adventure started when a dean at college told her, 'My dear, you want to be a scientist.' That changed everything. Harriet went to MIT, where there were hardly any women and almost no ladies' rooms! She studied how DNA, the instruction book inside all our cells, makes different types of cells. Later, she used chickens to study viruses that cause cancer. When she was 60, an age when many people retire, Harriet co-founded a company called GeoVax to work on an HIV vaccine. She also had three boys and proved you can be a great scientist and a mom. Her secret? She worked super efficiently from 9 to 5 and hired a housekeeper. Harriet's story shows that being different can be your superpower. So next time you feel like the odd one out, remember Harriet—the scientist who was just 'Harriet' but changed the world anyway.
why_it_matters: Harriet's story reminds you that even when you feel left out or different, you can still do amazing things and change the world.

keywords.explanation: An exhibition is a big show where many things or people come to show something cool.
A dean is a person in charge of a part of a college or university.
DNA is like a tiny instruction book inside every living thing's cells.
Viruses are tiny germs that can make you sick by entering your cells.
Co-founded means started a company or project together with someone else.
A vaccine is a special medicine that teaches your body to fight off a disease before you get sick.

background_read: In the 1960s, very few women became scientists. Many universities didn't even allow women to study certain sciences.
MIT (the Massachusetts Institute of Technology) is one of the world's top schools for science and engineering.
An HIV vaccine is something scientists have been trying to create for decades to stop a virus that can lead to AIDS.
Article_Structure: WHO: Harriet Robinson, a scientist who was often the only woman in a room of men.
WHAT: She was called by her first name while men were called 'Doctor' or 'Professor', but she went on to study DNA and viruses, and help create a company for an HIV vaccine.
WHERE: She worked at an exhibition in Moscow, studied at MIT (a university in the US), and later co-founded GeoVax.
WHY: Her story shows that you don't have to fit in to do important things; being different can be a strength.

perspectives.description: Harriet didn't let being called 'Harriet' stop her; she kept working hard and reached her goals.
Some people might think it was unfair that she wasn't given the same title as men, and that everyone should be treated equally.
Harriet shows that you can be a scientist and a mom, breaking the idea that you have to choose one path.
